ProgramName: Doctor of Education in Curriculum and Instruction, Elementary Education
Requirements: For the Ph.D. in Curriculum and Instruction, applicants are expected to have a master's degree in education or a related field, a minimum graduate GPA of 3.3, and at least three years of relevant professional experience. The application requires a resume/CV, a statement of purpose, a writing sample, and three letters of recommendation. The statement of purpose should outline your academic and professional background, research interests, and career goals, and also identify one or two faculty members whose research aligns with your interests. The writing sample should be a single-authored scholarly piece. GRE scores are not required for admission.
Description: The Ph.D. Program in Curriculum and Instruction is designed to develop scholarly leaders who can creatively and critically address the myriad of challenges and possibilities in education. With a focus on research, theory, and practice, the program prepares graduates for roles as university faculty, researchers, and leaders in a variety of educational institutions. Students in the program engage in rigorous inquiry, exploring diverse perspectives on curriculum, teaching, and learning. The program is tailored to individual interests, allowing students to work closely with faculty to design a course of study and research that aligns with their professional goals.

ProgramName: Doctor of Education in Educational Leadership and Policy Studies
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Human Sciences
Description: The Educational Leadership and Policy Studies a leading program designed for aspiring educational leaders and future faculty in educational leadership and policy studies. [7] The vast majority of our doctoral students pursue the Ed.D., though a Ph.D. option is available. For over fifty years, the Virginia Tech Educational Leadership and Policy Studies Parental Program has prepared aspiring educational administrators throughout the Commonwealth. Ed.D. graduates leave with the skills they need to lead ethically; advance equity and social justice in educational settings; consider and implement educational policy; lead innovative practices; communicate with diverse constituents; and improve the learning and well-being of all PK-12 students. [6, 9] The program is designed for working professionals, our programs can be completed on a part- or full-time basis, with coursework that incorporates modern theories with real-life practice. [7]
Accredidation: Our Educational Leadership & Policy Studies Program is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation. Since 2015, the program has been a member of the University Council for Educational Administration (UCEA), a consortium of higher education institutions committed to the advancement of educational leadership. [2]

ProgramName: Doctor of Education in Integrative STEM Education
Requirements: A master's degree from an accredited college or university with an earned GPA of 3.3 (on a 4.0 scale). [1] Three letters of recommendation are required. [1] Once your graduate school application is accepted, the program leader will contact you for a faculty interview (either face-to-face or online). [1]
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Human Sciences
Description: The Integrative STEM Education Doctoral program (Ed. D. or Ph. D.) Is designed for students who already hold a Master's Degree in education or STEM fields. [1] Either of the Ed. D. or Ph. D. programs will help you build on your existing knowledge and experience as you expand your understanding of STEM education by researching aspects related to integrative strategies for teaching STEM concepts. [1] This degree path is best suited for students who are interested in pursuing a career in fields related to educational research, postsecondary education, teacher education, or educational leadership and administration. [1] In the Integrative STEM Education Doctoral program, we emphasize the interconnectedness of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics disciplines as we help our students explore teaching and learning methods. [1] Real-world problems are rarely limited to a single school subject, and, as educators, we must help our students develop the ability to transfer skills and knowledge among subjects. [1] This holistic and integrative approach to teaching and learning is both more effective and more fun, for both teachers and students alike. [1] The Ed. D. is an applied degree, for those interested in leadership roles outside of academia. [1]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Aerospace Engineering

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Alliance for Social, Political, Ethical, and Cultural Thought
Requirements: A master's degree with minimum GPA 3.5 (4 Scale); Overall GPA 3.3 (4 Scale) in undergraduate education; TOEFL /IELTS Required (If Applicable). [3, 7] Students may apply to ASPECT on the basis of actual completion of an M.A degree or equivalent (e.g., M.S, M.Arch., M.B.A., or J.D.) or of the promise that an M.A. degree or equivalent will be obtained prior to entering the ASPECT Ph.D. program. [7]
Department: College of Liberal Arts and Human Sciences
Concentration: ['Social Thought and Theory', 'Political Thought and Theory', 'Ethical Thought and Theory', 'Cultural Thought and Theory']
Description: The ASPECT Ph. D. program fosters a critical engagement between domains of inquiry in the humanities, the social sciences, and the arts. [13] We bring together theoretical and empirical cross-disciplinary methodologies, concepts, salient issues, and analytical perspectives generated by ethical thought, cultural studies, political economy, social and political theory, intellectual history, critical world order studies, and aesthetics, performance arts and visual studies. [3] The Ph. D. curriculum concentrates on methodological and theoretical issues, as well as domains where social, political, ethical, and cultural thought are put to work in understanding social and individual transformations in contemporary and historical contexts. [3] Students pursuing the ASPECT Ph. D. select a major and a minor concentration chosen from among four areas: 1) social thought, 2) political thought, 3) ethical thought, and 4) cultural thought. [3] Additional ASPECT courses requirements offer education in interdisciplinary theory, methodology, and professional development. [3]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Animal Science
Requirements: The School of Animal Sciences Graduate Program uses a holistic approach to admission. Our recommended metrics include an overall GPA of 3.0 and the GRE is encouraged with scores of 150 verbal and quantitative. The VT Graduate School requires a TOEFL score of 90. Materials are uploaded through the Graduate School portal. [16]
Department: School of Animal Sciences
Fees: In-state: $19,218/Year, Out-of-state: $36,212/Year
Concentration: ['animal behavior & welfare', 'livestock business management', 'equine science', 'animal breeding and genetics', 'reproductive physiology', 'neurophysiology', 'embryology', 'nutrition', 'biotechnology']
Description: To prepare for the wide variety of career opportunities in animal and poultry sciences, students choose from one of three options: animal behavior, pre-vet, or no option. These options incorporate studies in areas such as animal behavior & welfare, livestream stock-business management, equine science, animal breeding and genetics, reproductive physiology, neurophysiology, embryology, nutrition, and biotechnology. The curriculum combines applications of biological sciences with significant hands-on experience, along with opportunities to work on the campus livestock and poultry research units and in the labs. Students also choose to study one or more groups of animals such as companion animal, equine, poultry, or livestock (beef cattle, sheep, and swine). Careers are available in science, business, and animal agriculture, as well as pre-professional preparation for veterinary medicine, medical school, graduate school, etc., in physiology, genetics, nutrition, behavior, or biotechnology.
CostPerCredit: In-state: $876, Out-of-state: $1,760
ScholarshipType: teaching or research assistantships, scholarships, external fellowships, fellowships tied to a specific institution, or loans

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Animal Sciences and Husbandry

Description: The School of Animal Sciences Graduate Program offers several degrees in multiple disciplines with programs of study tailored to fit the career objectives and interests of the students. [9] Our graduate students have diverse backgrounds and research interests with opportunities to conduct basic, applied, and computational research. [9] Additionally, graduate students have the the opportunity to gain classroom teaching experience and to participate in extension education programs along with their involvement in research programs. [9] The School resides in Litton-Reaves Hall, a modern, well-equipped, office building. [9] In addition to offices, it includes extensive laboratory and classroom facilities designed to support research, teaching, and extension programs. [9]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Architecture
Requirements: In addition to the Virginia Tech Graduate School application requirements, applicants must have a master's degree in a closely allied field and must submit a portfolio and a 2,500-word statement of research focus. [10]
Department: School of Architecture, School of Design

[26] An annual supplemental fee is also assessed to all graduate students majoring in Architecture and Design Research. [42]
Description: The Ph.D. in Architecture and Design Research is a research-only degree offered through the College of Architecture, Arts, and Design. The program is for students who want to contribute to the body of knowledge in the disciplines of architecture, landscape architecture, industrial design, and interior design. The Ph.D. program is STEM-designated, with a curriculum that is structured to provide a foundation in research methods and the development of a dissertation that makes an original contribution to the field. Ph.D. students benefit from the diverse expertise of the faculty and the resources of a leading research university. The program encourages interdisciplinary research and collaboration with other departments and research centers at Virginia Tech.
MinimumGreScore: Verbal: 154 or better; Quantitative: 152 or better
ScholarshipType: The School of Architecture offers a one-time 'Technology Support Fund' scholarship based on financial need. [40]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Biochemistry
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Description: The Ph.D. program in the Department of Biochemistry at Virginia Tech prepares students for careers as independent researchers in biochemistry, molecular and cellular biology, molecular microbiology, biotechnology, and related areas. [3] The program emphasizes mentored dissertation research with the goal of training students to become capable, ethical, and independent researchers. [3] Coursework is typically completed within the first two years, with the remainder of the time focused on research. [3] The first year includes research rotations in three different faculty laboratories, coursework, journal clubs, and seminars. [3] Students select a dissertation advisor in late November of their first year and begin dissertation work in December. [3] A Qualifying Examination is required at the end of the first year, and a Preliminary Examination is required at the end of the second year. [3] The rest of the program is dedicated to research, journal clubs, and seminars, culminating in a written dissertation and oral defense. [3]

A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Three letters of recommendation. A written statement of intent/personal statement for pursuing graduate studies. TOEFL, IELTS, or IBT For applicants whose native language is not English, satisfactory scores from a standardized test of English Language Proficiency is required. [1]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Business with a concentration in Business Information Technology
Requirements: A complete application consists of the following items: A completed online application; GRE or GMAT scores (less than 5 years old) in 90th percentile (95th or higher is preferable). TOEFL (if required) scores sent to Virginia Tech; ETS Institution Code 5859. TOEFL score of 90 (IBT) or an IELTS score of 6.5 for admission; TOEFL scores of 20 or greater in Listening, Writing, Speaking, and Reading subsections are required. Students who anticipate appointment as Graduate Teaching Assistants are expected to have scored 25 or greater on the TOEFL Speaking subtest. Master's degree (unless one has exceptional research, work, or undergraduate record) with a GPA of 3.70 or higher. Undergraduate degree GPA of 3.50 or higher; Official transcripts of undergraduate and graduate course work and letters of recommendation should be sent to the Graduate School. [1]
Department: Pamplin College of Business
Description: The Business Information Technology (BIT) PhD program at Virginia Tech is a highly innovative and interdisciplinary program that prepares students to become leading faculty members in top-tier research universities. [5] The program's STEM-based curriculum fuses operations management, supply chain management, management information systems, information systems, artificial intelligence, business analytics, decision science, and information technology. [5, 7] The BIT PhD curriculum is designed to fuse three primary areas of learning: (1) IS, operations management, and security discipline foundations; (2) science, theory, publishing, and career foundations; and (3) AI, ML, Analytics, and behavioral economics foundations. [6] All these areas are supported by broader interdisciplinary training, aiming to produce breakthrough combinations and research in interdisciplinary frontiers. [6] The program aims to tackle “Grand Challenges,” significant global problems requiring innovative societal, business, technology, and government transformations. [6]
Accredidation: The Pamplin College of Business, which offers the Ph.D. program, is accredited by The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) International. [4, 9] This accreditation applies to the undergraduate, master's, and Ph.D. programs in business. [9]
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition waiver and a competitive stipend

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Chemistry
Requirements: Applicants need to provide transcripts of all colleges attended, with the Graduate School at Virginia Tech rarely admitting students with GPAs less than 3.0. [5] Additionally, a statement of purpose, 3 letters of recommendation, and an updated CV are required. [8]
Department: College of Science
Description: The Ph.D. in Chemistry is the highest degree offered in the department and is keenly focused on the development of research skills. The program's central component is the doctoral dissertation, which is an original and significant contribution to the body of chemical knowledge. Students will work in close-knit apprenticeship relationships with faculty who are leaders in their fields, and who are working at the very edge of discovery in the chemical sciences. Students typically complete this degree in five years.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Civil Engineering
Requirements: Admission for graduate study in Civil and Environmental Engineering at Virginia Tech is granted by the Graduate School, upon recommendation of the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department. Admission normally requires a bachelor's degree in engineering from an ABET-accredited engineering program. [3] A GPA of 3.00 or higher (on a 4.0 scale) for the last 60 semester hours is typically required. [6] Those without an engineering background must complete background courses or show proficiency in fundamental areas such as math, science, and engineering science. [4] Applicants must upload a copy of their official transcript into the online application. [3]
Department: College of Engineering

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Computer and Information Sciences
Requirements: For direct-entry Ph.D. admissions, a bachelor's degree in computer science or a related area is required, with a minimum 3.5 GPA. GREs are not required. For regular Ph.D. admissions (for those with a master's degree), a master's degree in computer science or a related area is required. The master's degree should be from a U.S. university or a recognized international equivalent, with a 3.5 GPA in the master's program. For all applicants, three letters of recommendation are required, and a resume and statement of purpose must also be submitted. International students may need to submit TOEFL scores.
Department: College of Engineering

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Counselor Education and Supervision
Requirements: Doctoral program admission requirements include a master's degree in Counselor Education or a closely related field, including a counseling practicum and internship experience. Applicants with degrees in other counseling fields (i.e., Marriage and Family Therapy, Counseling Psychology) are considered but may be required to complete the CACREP master's degree core courses that were not included in their degrees. Applicants with at least two years of post-masters counseling experience are given the strongest consideration. Minimum 3.0 GPA in the master's program. Three letters of recommendation are required. Include a scanned copy of your official transcripts with your online application, then arrange for an official copy to be sent to both Graduate Admissions and School of Education after you receive an offer of admission.
Department: School of Education
Description: The Virginia Tech Counselor Education Ph.D. program prepares students to function as counselor educators, clinical supervisors, or advanced clinicians, through coursework, research, and practical training. [3] The doctoral program in Counseling Education and Supervision is offered on our Blacksburg campus, and prepares skilled counselors who conduct impactful research, practice, supervise, and teach. [9] Our program strongly endorses the researcher-practitioner model. Our students receive a strong foundation in research methods that help them to design and conduct research that can be translated into practice. [8] Doctoral students in the Virginia Tech program have access to the latest instructional technologies, work closely with the faculty, and often collaborate on research, publications, and conference presentations. [8]
Accredidation: Our Counselor Education Programs are accredited by the Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP). [9] They are also approved by the Virginia Department of Education for the preparation of school counselors. [9]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Crop & Soil Environmental Sciences

Description: The School of Plant and Environmental Sciences offers PhD and MS degrees in three programs: Crop and Soil Environmental Sciences; Horticulture; and Plant Pathology, Physiology, and Weed Science. A scholarly writing sample in English (e.g., a master's thesis, article, or academic paper) is required for application to a doctoral program. [1]
Description: The Educational Psychology faculty offer a Ph.D. program in Curriculum and Instruction with a specialization in Educational Psychology. Students are prepared conspiracies and research positions in academic environments such as colleges, universities and school districts. Our doctoral program provides a context for graduate education that is focused on theory, research, practice, innovation, inquiry, and equity. [2] The program emphasizes the research and theories related to learning and motivation, as well as how to apply the research and theories to practice. Students in the Educational Psychology Doctoral Program study learning, development, motivation, assessment, testing, and instructional design. [2] Individualized programs of study are developed for students to ensure that their studies prepare them well for the career paths they choose. [2]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Curriculum and Instruction, Elementary Education
Requirements: An appropriate master's-level degree from an accredited institution; Qualify for admission to the Graduate School; A GPA of 3.0 or above in one's graduate work; At least 3 years of experience teaching in grades K-12; TOEFL/ IELTS (For all non-U.S. citizens or non-U.S. permanent residents). [3]
Department: School of Education
Description: The PhD track in elementary education is designed to help students contribute to the advancement of knowledge needed to address the dynamic challenges of contemporary education at the elementary level. The program trains leaders in educational research and encourages students to delve deep into their own research areas. Key emphases of the program include a focus on interdisciplinary approaches to curriculum development, the use of inquiry as a primary pedagogical approach, the importance of a strong understanding of diversity and its social and educational implications, and the role of child development and learning theories as a foundation for research and teaching in elementary settings. Students are prepared for teaching and research positions in academic environments like colleges and universities, as well as in school districts. The program provides a context for graduate education focused on theory, research, practice, innovation, inquiry, and equity. [1, 2]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Curriculum and Instruction, History and Social Science Education
Requirements: Applicants must have a Master's degree with a grade point average of 3.0 or above in graduate work. A completed Graduate School application is necessary, along with three professional letters of recommendation. An interview with the admissions committee is also required. Applicants should have relevant teaching experience, defined as three or more years of K-12 teaching or other significant teaching experience. [1]
Department: School of Education
Description: The School of Education at Virginia Tech offers a doctoral program in Curriculum and Instruction with emphasis in History and Social Science Education. [1] The doctoral program is made up of full time and part-time doctoral students. [1] Every effort is made to secure graduate assistantships for full-time students as they complete their one-year academic residency requirement. [1] Students are expected to complete doctoral examinations and dissertation including qualifying exam, preliminary exam, prospectus and final examination. [1] The History and Social Science Education Doctoral Program emphasizes the following strands of research pertaining to History and Social Science: Comparative studies of history and social science education, Education of preservice and in-service teachers, How students learn history and social science, The role of multimedia and technology to support historical inquiry, Curriculum History, Citizenship Education, Teaching and Learning with and About Difficult Knowledge / History informal and informal setting, and Learning and Assessment in Social Studies. [1] The History and Social Science Education Doctoral Program is primarily designed to prepare researchers and higher education faculty. [1] The possible career paths could be but not limited to faculty positions in post-secondary education and for leadership positions in secondary education. [1] The History and Social Science Education Doctoral Program at Virginia Tech is designed to prepare reflective educators who are ready, willing, and able to facilitate the type of systematic critical literacy work that is a vital part of preparing 21st century citizens to become thoughtful and nuanced readers of the word and the world, both past and present. [1]
ScholarshipType: Dan B. Fleming Jr. Endowed Scholarship in History and Social Science Education, Assistantships, Fellowships

Description: The Integrative STEM Education Doctoral program (Ph.D.) is designed for students who already hold a Master's Degree in education or STEM fields. It helps students build on their existing knowledge and experience as they expand their understanding of STEM education by researching aspects related to integrative strategies for teaching STEM concepts. The Ph.D. is considered a research-focused degree for those who are interested in pursuing a career in academia where the conduct of research would be an integral part of one's position. [1]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Educational Administration

[6] Application materials include transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a writing sample, a letter of interest and curriculum vitae/resume, and an interview with faculty. [6] GRE scores are not required. [6]

Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Educational Leadership and Policy Studies is designed for individuals who wish to pursue careers in university teaching or in policy-related work. The program focuses on developing advanced research and analytical skills for educational leaders, emphasizing the intersection of leadership, policy, and practice to address educational challenges. Students engage in critical inquiries related to equity, inclusiveness, and systemic change in educational settings. The curriculum includes coursework in governance and policy, quantitative and qualitative research methods, literature reviews, advanced school law, advanced school finance, legal aspects of special education, theories of educational administration, and more. An individual program of studies is planned for each student based on their academic background and interests.
Accredidation: The Educational Leadership & Policy Studies Program is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Educational Leadership and Policy Studies

Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) program in Educational Leadership & Policy Studies (ELPS) (EPS), with provisions for educational leadership, including special education administration, is designed for a person who is anticipating an academic career or in an area of practice which demands theoretical research expertise; who is interested in theory and conceptual analysis; and is interested in research which has potential for advancing education theory and practice. [1] As a member of the Educational Leadership and Policy Studies program, you will develop the knowledge, skills, and dispositions necessary to transform teaching and learning, conduct groundbreaking research, and engage with and lead learning communities at home and around the globe. Reimagining the future of education begins with educational leadership practices that put educational excellence, innovation, and equity at the fore. [6]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Electrical Engineering
Requirements: Admission requirements for the Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering at Virginia Tech include an undergraduate degree in engineering or physical sciences, TOEFL/IELTS scores for applicants from countries where English is not the primary language, a curriculum vitae or resume, transcripts from each post-secondary institution, a statement of intent, and at least three letters of recommendation. Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) is the highest academic degree awarded by the university and is conferred upon students who demonstrate outstanding original scholarship during advanced study. [9] It signifies that the student is able to conduct independent research and has both a broad basic knowledge of all areas of the field and a comprehensive knowledge of one area. [9] Each Ph.D. student must complete a minimum of 92 credit hours, consisting of 30 course-credit hours, 60 credit-hours of research and dissertation, and 2 course-credit-hours of Seminar. [9] The PhD program in Electrical Engineering is designed for students who want to deepen their knowledge and advance research in the field. [8] It offers a flexible yet rigorous curriculum that emphasizes original research, preparing students to contribute to technological innovations. [8] Students applying for the Ph.D. program typically have a masters degree from an accredited college or university in EE, CPE, or a related field. ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in English Education
Requirements: Master's degree. Grade point average of 3.0 or above in graduate work. A completed Graduate School application. Three professional letters of recommendation, e.g. professors or relevant educational employers. An interview with the English Education admissions committee, including a discussion of the application folio and other related issues. Relevant teaching experience: Three or more years of teaching English in the middle or high school level (grades 6-12). [3]
Department: School of Education, College of Liberal Arts and Human Sciences
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy in Curriculum and Instruction with an emphasis in English Education at Virginia Tech is primarily designed to prepare researchers, English/Literacy teacher education faculty, and Literacy Curriculum Coaches. [3] The program prepares English teachers, teacher educators, and scholars to be successful in the context of increasingly standardized education reforms. [3, 9] Working from the perspective that learning should be a generative act, faculty guide students in the exploration of concepts that make student-centered, dialogic approaches central constructs in the study of teaching and learning. [3, 9] Courses focus on literacy development and consider the roles of language and culture in approaches to teaching that bring classroom content into dialogue with students' lives in 21st century classrooms. [3, 9] The program emphasizes several research strands, including Dialogic approaches to teaching and learning, New literacies and adolescent learning, Adolescent literacy, The study of literature and writing in K-12 contexts, Literacy development, and Critical literacy. [3] Please note, the program's website states that it is undergoing restructuring and is not currently accepting new students. [13]
Accredidation: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University is institutionally accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools, Commission on Colleges. [14] No specific accreditation for the Doctor of Philosophy in English Education program is mentioned on the university's website. [14]

Requirements: Guidelines for evaluating students include the application, prior grades (minimum 3.4/4.0 GPA for Doctoral applicants) and coursework, TOEFL for foreign students only, research and job experiences, and recommendation letters. [8] All graduate students are required to demonstrate competency in basic insect biology and statistics prior to graduation. [8]

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Environmental Design & Planning

[5] The curriculum requires coursework to develop student knowledge of programming computers to analyze large-scale data sets from social media platforms. [5] Students will gain an understanding of principles and techniques for big data analytics, including methods for storing, searching, retrieving, and processing large data sets. [5] Students will learn how to gather and analyze data from social media networks (e.g., Twitter, Facebook, Linkedln) and program the computer to use the resulting information to make predictions of future outcomes. The program focuses on extracting information from large data sets, as well as analyzing and solving problems by modeling, simulation, and optimization, drawing on the computational skills that make solving the complex problems of the 21st century possible. In addition to the standard degree option, CMDA offers specialized options in: Biological Sciences, Cryptography & Cybersecurity, Economics, Geosciences, and Physics.
